mainTopic: Whether the first קדושה of ירושלים and the בית המקדש lasts forever, and what that means for adding to the holy areas
overview: The daf first finishes an earlier point: at the ceremony for adding to ירושלים, a נביא decided which תודה loaves were eaten and which were burned. Then רב הונא and רב נחמן argue about the wording of the משנה. רב הונא reads 'with all these' procedures, and רב נחמן reads 'with one of all these.' Behind this is a bigger question: did the first קדושה of the בית המקדש last forever, or did it end when the first בית המקדש was destroyed, so that עזרא had to make it holy again? A ברייתא of אבא שאול about two ponds on the Mount of Olives seems to prove that every procedure is needed. The גמרא answers that this is a מחלוקת between תנאים, and it tries to show that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree. רבינא suggests they may not really disagree. So the גמרא brings רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who says the first walled cities lost their status in the exile. A second ברייתא in his name says the opposite. The גמרא resolves this in two ways: either two תנאים reported his view differently, or one teaching really belongs to his brother רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.

steps.title: A prophet decided which loaves were eaten and which were burned
steps.stepSummary: This closes the earlier discussion about the two תודה loaves used when adding to ירושלים. Whether a loaf was eaten or burned was decided by a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: By the word of a prophet one was eaten, and by the word of a prophet one was burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier point. It says the decision about which תודה loaves to eat and which to burn came from a נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No logical reason is given for treating the two loaves differently. The practice rested on a נביא's instruction. This wraps up the earlier discussion before the גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: By the word or instruction of a prophet

phrases.english: By the word of a prophet it was eaten
phrases.notes: 'It' is one of the תודה loaves from the ceremony of adding to the city.

phrases.english: and by the word of a prophet it was burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל פִּי נָבִיא נֶאֱכֶלֶת וְעַל פִּי נָבִיא נִשְׂרֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section, about how they knew which תודה loaf to eat and which to burn.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The eating or burning of the תודה loaves was decided by a נביא's instruction, not by a stated reason.

steps.title: Two versions of the משנה: all procedures or just one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about additions made without 'all these' procedures. רב הונא and רב נחמן disagree about how the line reads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: any addition not made with all these procedures does not become holy. It was stated that the אמוראים disagree. רב הונא says we learned 'with all these.' רב נחמן says we learned 'with one of all these.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה and reports a disagreement about its exact wording. One reading says every procedure is needed, and the other says any one procedure is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב הונא's wording, missing even one procedure means the added area is not holy. With רב נחמן's wording, doing any one of the listed procedures is enough. The next two steps explain the reasoning behind each reading.

keyTerms.meaning: With one of all these procedures

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just an argument about one word. The choice between 'all' and 'one' decides whether every procedure is required. It also connects to a bigger question about the בית המקדש's קדושה, which comes in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֵׂית בְּכׇל אֵלּוּ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Any addition that was not made with all these, etc.
phrases.notes: 'All these' points back to the משנה's list: a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, the court of 71, the two תודות, and song.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna says:
We learned 'with all these,'
Rav Naḥman says:
We learned 'with one of all these.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: בְּכׇל אֵלּוּ תְּנַן, רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בְּאַחַת מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תודה loaves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: every procedure is required. רב נחמן: any one procedure is enough.

steps.title: רב הונא's reason: the first holiness lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that the first קדושה of the בית המקדש lasted forever. So what עזרא did was only a reminder, and his ceremony proves nothing about missing procedures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says we learned 'with all these,' because he holds the first קדושה made the place holy for its own time and for the future. עזרא only did a ceremony as a reminder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא can say every procedure is needed. In his view, the place never lost its first קדושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might ask how the second בית המקדש was holy if עזרא lacked some procedures. רב הונא answers that it was already holy from the first קדושה, which never ended. So עזרא's ceremony was only a commemoration, and it does not show that fewer procedures are enough for a new holy area.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; introduces someone's underlying view
The first consecration (in the time of the first בית המקדש)

phrases.english: Rav Huna says we learned 'with all these' —
he holds that the first consecration
sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future,
and Ezra merely did it as a remembrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר בְּכׇל אֵלּוּ תְּנַן – קָסָבַר קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב הונא's reading from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first קדושה is permanent, so עזרא's ceremony was only a commemoration and all procedures are needed for a truly new consecration.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a wording question in the משנה to a major question: does the בית המקדש site stay holy even after its destruction?

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason: עזרא truly consecrated without the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that the first קדושה lasted only for its own time. So עזרא really did make the place holy again, even without the אורים ותומים. This proves not every procedure is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says we learned 'with one of all these,' because he holds the first קדושה made the place holy only for its time and not for the future. עזרא truly consecrated it, even though there were no אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב נחמן's reading. Since עזרא's consecration was real and worked without the אורים ותומים, one procedure must be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the first קדושה ended when the first בית המקדש was destroyed. So the second בית המקדש's holiness came only from עזרא's ceremony. That ceremony worked even though the אורים ותומים were missing, which shows that not all the procedures are required.

keyTerms.meaning: The אורים ותומים in the כהן גדול's breastplate, missing in the second בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the first קדושה lasts forever, so עזרא only commemorated, and all procedures are required. רב נחמן: the first קדושה ended, so עזרא truly consecrated without the אורים ותומים, and one procedure is enough.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר ״בְּאַחַת מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ״ תְּנַן –
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says we learned 'with one of all these' —
he holds that the first consecration
sanctified for its time
and did not sanctify for the future,
and Ezra truly consecrated it

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הֲווֹ אוּרִים וְתוּמִּים.
phrases.english: even though there were no Urim VeTummim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר בְּאַחַת מִכׇּל אֵלּוּ תְּנַן – קָסָבַר: קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְלֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 3, giving the opposite view of the first קדושה and of עזרא's ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first קדושה was temporary, so עזרא's consecration without the אורים ותומים was real, which shows one procedure is enough.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה's words
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה says 'with all these,' which sounds like every procedure is required. That goes against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן: The משנה says, 'Any addition that was not made with all these procedures'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן using the plain words of the משנה. The משנה says 'with ALL these.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said in Step 4 that not every procedure is needed, since עזרא made the place holy without אורים ותומים. But the משנה says an addition not made 'with all these' is not holy, which means all of them are needed. So the משנה's own wording seems to go against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: With all these, meaning all the procedures listed in the משנה

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
"Any [addition] that was not made with all these"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's position from Step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that not every procedure is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says 'with ALL these,' so it sounds like every procedure is required.

steps.title: רב נחמן rereads the משנה as 'one of all these'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה should be read as 'with one of all these.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'With one of all these procedures.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers by changing how the line in the משנה is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the משנה is only saying that an addition made with none of these procedures is not holy. If even one was used, as with עזרא, the addition can work. This fits his view that not every procedure is required.

keyTerms.meaning: With one of all these procedures

phrases.english: Teach it as: "with one of all these."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires every single procedure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that at least one of the procedures is needed.

steps.title: אבא שאול's two ponds on the Mount of Olives
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It says the upper pond was made holy by עולי גולה without a מלך and without אורים ותומים, and so it did not get full קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: אבא שאול says: There were two ponds on the Mount of Olives, a lower one and an upper one. The lower one was made holy with all these procedures. The upper one was not made holy with all these procedures. It was made holy only by those who came back from exile, without a מלך and without the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רב נחמן with a ברייתא. This step sets up the two ponds, and the next steps will spell out their laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper pond is just like עזרא's case: it was made holy by עולי גולה, with no מלך and no אורים ותומים. The ברייתא says it was 'not made holy with all these,' and we will see its קדושה was not complete. That sounds against רב נחמן, who said such a ceremony really works.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who came back from the Babylonian exile, in the days of עזרא
The holy oracle in the כהן גדול's breastplate

steps.confusionAlert: Both ponds were areas added to ירושלים. The difference is HOW each one was treated: the lower one got all the procedures, and the upper one did not, so it never got full קדושה.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Abba Shaul says:
There were two ponds on the Mount of Olives,
a lower one and an upper one.
The lower one was made holy with all these;
the upper one was not made holy with all these,
but rather by those who came up from the exile;
without a king and without the Urim veTumim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן's answer, a new source is brought against him
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that עזרא's ceremony worked without all the procedures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A place made holy by עולי גולה without a מלך or אורים ותומים is described as not properly made holy.

steps.title: The lower pond had full holiness
steps.stepSummary: In the lower pond, which had full קדושה, the careful חברים ate both קדשים קלים and מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lower pond, whose holiness was complete: עמי הארץ would go in there and eat קדשים קלים there, but not מעשר שני. And חברים would eat both קדשים קלים and מעשר שני there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and describes how people acted in the lower pond, which was fully holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key group is the חברים, the people who are careful about these laws. They ate both קדשים קלים and מעשר שני there, which shows they treated it as real ירושלים. This sets up the contrast with the upper pond.

keyTerms.meaning: People who were not careful about laws like מעשרות and טהרה
People who were careful about those laws
Offerings of lesser holiness, which may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים
Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: The lower one, whose holiness was complete:
amei haaretz would go in there,
and eat lesser-sanctity offerings there
but not second tithe;
and chaverim would eat there
lesser-sanctity offerings and second tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the laws of the lower pond
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lower pond had full קדושה, and חברים ate both קדשים קלים and מעשר שני there.

steps.title: The upper pond did not have full holiness
steps.stepSummary: In the upper pond, the חברים would not eat קדשים קלים or מעשר שני. This shows it was not treated as real ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The upper pond, whose holiness was not complete: עמי הארץ would go in there and eat קדשים קלים there, but not מעשר שני. But חברים would eat neither קדשים קלים nor מעשר שני there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes the upper pond, which was made holy without all the procedures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The careful חברים refused to eat any holy food there. That shows the upper pond did not truly have the קדושה of ירושלים. Only the less careful עמי הארץ ate קדשים קלים there.

phrases.english: The upper one, whose holiness was not complete:
amei haaretz would go in there,
and eat lesser-sanctity offerings there
but not second tithe;
but chaverim would not eat there

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים וְלֹא מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: neither lesser-sanctity offerings nor second tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the upper pond with the lower pond
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upper pond did not have full קדושה, so חברים ate no holy food there.

steps.title: Why the upper pond was not made holy: every procedure is needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the upper pond was not made holy because additions need a מלך, נביא, אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of 71, two תודות and a song. That sounds directly against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they not make it holy? Because additions to the city and to the courtyards are made only with a מלך, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, a סנהדרין of seventy-one, two תודות and a song.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the reason the upper pond was not holy. This line is the sharp edge of the challenge against רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that additions are made 'only' with the full list of procedures. Since עולי גולה had no מלך or אורים ותומים, their ceremony did not work. This contradicts רב נחמן's claim that עזרא truly made the place holy without them.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not add, meaning additions cannot be made
The courtyards of the בית המקדש
Two תודה offerings, whose loaves were used in the ceremony

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of אבא שאול says a place made holy by עולי גולה, without a מלך and אורים ותומים, did not get full קדושה, because every procedure is needed. This is a strong challenge to רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move: רב נחמן must explain how this ברייתא fits his view that עזרא's ceremony really worked.

phrases.english: And for what reason did they not make it holy?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל הָעִיר וְעַל הָעֲזָרוֹת
phrases.english: Because additions are not made to the city or to the courtyards
except with a king, a prophet and the Urim veTumim,
and with a Sanhedrin of seventy-one,
and with two thanks-offerings and with song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the upper pond's incomplete קדושה and completes the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view, and his rereading of the משנה as 'one of all these'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says additions need the full list of procedures, and a ceremony by עולי גולה without a מלך and אורים ותומים did not work.

steps.title: Why did they make the upper pond holy?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the upper pond was made holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why did they make it holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question about the upper pond. It is setting up the next move, where the question itself gets corrected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just heard that the upper pond did not get full קדושה. So the natural question is why they bothered with it at all. As we will see, the way this question is worded is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: But why did they make it holy?
phrases.notes: "It" is the upper pond from the ברייתא in the steps before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the upper pond, which step 10 said was not made holy.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the purpose of the upper pond, if it was never properly made holy?

steps.title: Correcting the question: why did they bring it inside the walls?
steps.stepSummary: The question contradicts itself, since we just said they did not make it holy. So it is reworded as: why did they include it inside the city?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they make it holy?! Didn't you just say they did not make it holy? Rather, ask: why did they bring it inside the city?
steps.whatsHappening: The question in step 11 is pushed back on because of its wording. Then it is restated in a form that makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot ask 'why did they make it holy' about something that was not made holy. The real puzzle is a different one. If the pond would not be holy, why was it put inside the walls of ירושלים at all?

phrases.english: Why did they make it holy?!
But you said they did not make it holy!
Rather, why did they bring it inside?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה קִידְּשׁוּהָ הָא אָמְרַתְּ לֹא קִידְּשׁוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and rewords the question of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the question in step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question takes for granted that the pond was made holy, which goes against what was just said.

steps.title: It was a weak spot in the city's defense
steps.stepSummary: They brought the upper pond inside the walls because it was a weak point through which the city could easily be captured.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it was the weak point of ירושלים, and the city was easy to conquer from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the corrected question. The reason was safety, not holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the pond inside the walls was a military decision. If it had been left outside, enemies could have attacked the city from there. So it was walled in, even though it never got the קדושה of ירושלים.
steps.whatToRemember: Being inside the walls of ירושלים does not by itself make a place holy. The upper pond was inside the walls only for defense.

phrases.english: Because it was the weak point of Jerusalem,
and it was easy to be conquered from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reworded question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was walled in for military protection, because it was the city's weak point.

steps.title: Defending רב נחמן: this is a מחלוקת between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב נחמן. The ברייתא follows one side of a מחלוקת between תנאים, and רב נחמן follows the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a disagreement between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the strong challenge against רב נחמן from step 10 and gives a short answer. It is setting up the proof that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of אבא שאול fits רב הונא's view: the first קדושה lasted forever, so עזרא's ceremony was only a reminder and could not make a new area like the upper pond holy. רב נחמן holds the first קדושה ended. He can follow the תנאים who say that, and on their view עזרא's ceremony truly made the place holy without every procedure.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a disagreement between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: This short line does not say who holds what. The next steps show the two opinions about whether the first קדושה lasted forever.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tannaim;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question about the pond to answer the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute: רב נחמן holds like a different תנא than the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that all the procedures are always needed, which goes against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the view that the first קדושה lasts forever, which is רב הונא's view. רב נחמן follows the תנאים who hold it ended.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: curtains were used while building
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reports that during the building of the second בית המקדש, they put up curtains around the היכל and around the courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר said, I heard that when they were building the היכל, they made curtains for the היכל and curtains for the courtyards. The difference was that for the היכל they built from outside the curtains, and for the courtyards they built from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first half of the source for the מחלוקת. This is רבי אליעזר's tradition about curtains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Curtains were put up to stand in place of the walls until the stone walls were finished. The workers did not go into the היכל, because of its great holiness. In the courtyards they were allowed to build from inside. The fact that curtains were needed will be used to suggest that, for רבי אליעזר, the holiness depended on having a wall.

keyTerms.meaning: the main building of the בית המקדש
the courtyards of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer said:
I heard that when they were building the Sanctuary,
they made curtains for the Sanctuary
and curtains for the courtyards.
Except that in the Sanctuary they build from outside,
and in the courtyards they build from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the מחלוקת mentioned in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a מחלוקת between תנאים about the first קדושה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תנא's teaching of רבי אליעזר (עדיות 8:6)

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the first קדושה lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says that קרבנות can be offered and holy food eaten even without the building, curtains or a wall, because the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I heard that we offer קרבנות even when there is no בית המקדש. We eat קדשי קדשים even when there are no curtains, and קדשים קלים and מעשר שני even when there is no wall. This is because the first קדושה made it holy for its own time and also for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second half of the source. This is רבי יהושע's tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the holiness of the place does not need any walls or buildings. The holiness from the first time stays forever. This matches רב הונא's view and the ברייתא of אבא שאול. רב נחמן, who holds the first קדושה ended, needs the other side of the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: the holiest קרבנות, eaten only in the courtyard
the first holiness (from the days of שלמה)

steps.whyThisMatters: "Did the first קדושה last forever?" is a big question. It affects whether the holy places of ירושלים and the בית המקדש still have their holiness after the חורבן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בַּיִת,
phrases.english: I heard that one offers sacrifices even though there is no Temple,
one eats offerings of the most sacred order
even though there are no curtains,
offerings of lesser sanctity and second tithe
even though there is no wall;
because the first sanctification sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future to come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same source with the second תנא's tradition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first קדושה lasts forever, so no building, curtains or wall are needed.

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר must hold the first קדושה ended
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהושע gives the reason 'it lasts forever,' this suggests that רבי אליעזר disagrees and holds it did not last forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this imply that רבי אליעזר holds it did not make it holy for the future?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the two traditions. It reads them as a real מחלוקת, which completes the defense of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's reason seems to be said against someone. That would be רבי אליעזר, who needed curtains. So there are two views. The ברייתא against רב נחמן fits רבי יהושע's side, and רב נחמן can follow רבי אליעזר, who holds the first קדושה ended.

phrases.english: Is it not by implication that Rabbi Eliezer holds:
It did not sanctify for the future to come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the two traditions in steps 15 and 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about whether the first קדושה lasts forever
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reason given by רבי יהושע, read as a reply to רבי אליעזר

steps.title: רבינא: maybe there is no מחלוקת at all
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how we know they disagree. Perhaps both hold the first קדושה lasts forever, and each one simply reported what he had heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: How do you know? Maybe everyone agrees that the first קדושה made it holy for its time and for the future. One חכם said what he heard, and the other חכם said what he heard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on the conclusion of step 17. He suggests the two traditions do not really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר only reported a fact: curtains were used. He never said that the holiness ended. So the two traditions can fit together. That weakens the claim that the תנאים disagree.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
From where do you know?
Perhaps everyone agrees
the first sanctification sanctified for its time
and sanctified for the future to come,
and one Sage said what he heard,
and the other Sage said what he heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 17 that the תנאים disagree.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The conclusion that רבי אליעזר holds the first קדושה ended
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A tradition about curtains does not show that he held the holiness ended. Each one may just be passing on what he heard.

steps.title: Then why did רבי אליעזר need curtains?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible problem with רבינא's approach. If the holiness never ended, why were curtains needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: according to רבי אליעזר, why do I need curtains?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a question against רבינא's suggestion. It is setting up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place stays holy without any walls, curtains add nothing to its holiness. Then the curtains seem to have no purpose. This question needs an answer for רבינא's reading to work.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
According to Rabbi Eliezer, why do I need curtains?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא קְלָעִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question against רבינא's reading in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that רבי אליעזר also holds the first קדושה lasts forever
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the holiness never ended, the curtains seem to serve no purpose.

steps.title: The curtains were only for privacy
steps.stepSummary: The curtains were not there to keep the place holy. They were only for privacy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just for privacy.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from step 19 is answered. This closes רבינא's argument that there may be no מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curtains had nothing to do with holiness. They simply kept the holy area from being seen by everyone. So רבי אליעזר can agree that the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tried to answer the challenge against רב נחמן by turning it into a מחלוקת between תנאים about the first קדושה. רבינא shows that the source used for this may not be a מחלוקת at all, since the curtains could have been just for privacy.

phrases.english: Merely for privacy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different purpose for the curtains
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curtains were needed to keep the place holy, so רבי אליעזר holds the holiness ended.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curtains were only for privacy, so they show nothing about whether the holiness ended.

steps.title: A תנא who says the first holiness ended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says the walled cities from יהושע's time lost their holiness when the land was emptied in exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, these תנאים argue about it. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said: Why did the חכמים list only these walled cities? Because when the exiles came back, they found these and made them holy. But the first ones lost their holiness when the land was emptied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves away from רבינא's idea that nobody disputes this. It shows a real תנא who seems to hold that the first holiness did not last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A walled city from יהושע's time has special laws, and it depends on the same question as ירושלים: does the first קדושה last forever? רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי says the original cities 'became nullified' in the exile. Only the ones made holy again by the returning exiles count.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the חכמים of the משנה period
The exiles who returned from בבל in the time of עזרא
They became nullified; they lost their status

phrases.english: Rather, these תנאים [argue about it] –

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
Why did the Sages list these?
phrases.notes: "These" are the walled cities listed in a משנה in ערכין.

phrases.english: Because when the exiles came up [to ארץ ישראל],
they found these and made them holy.
But the first ones lost their holiness
once the land was emptied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבינא's suggestion (step 18) by showing a different תנא who clearly disputes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original walled cities lost their status in the exile; only those the returning exiles found and made holy count.

steps.title: So he holds the first holiness was temporary
steps.stepSummary: From that ברייתא, the גמרא concludes that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds the first קדושה was only for its own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds: the first קדושה made things holy for its time, and not for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the clear lesson from the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cities lost their holiness in the exile, then the first holiness was not permanent. So here is a תנא who holds the opposite of 'it lasts forever.'

phrases.english: So it seems he holds:
the first holiness made things holy for its time
and did not make them holy for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא holds the first קדושה was only temporary.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's statement that the first walled cities became nullified.

steps.title: A second statement by the same תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a contradiction by quoting another ברייתא from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי about the walled cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they pointed out a contradiction: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said: Were these the only walled cities? Doesn't the פסוק say: 'Sixty cities, the whole region of ארגב, the kingdom of עוג in בשן, all these were cities fortified with a high wall'? So why did the חכמים list these? Because when the exiles came back, they found these and made them holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a contradiction. It begins quoting a second ברייתא in the name of the same תנא, and the clash will show up a few lines later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here he points out that there were many more walled cities, so the list in the משנה is not complete. The ברייתא continues in step 26, and that is where it clashes with step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: ורְמִינְהִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: And they pointed out a contradiction: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said:
Were these the only ones?!
But hasn't it already been said:
"Sixty cities, all the region of Argov,
the kingdom of Og in Bashan,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אֵלֶּה עָרִים בְּצֻרוֹת חוֹמָה גְבֹהָה״!
phrases.english: all these were cities fortified with a high wall"!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָמָּה מָנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת אֵלּוּ –
phrases.english: So why did the Sages list these?
Because when the exiles came up,
they found these and made them holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורְמִינְהִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a contradiction against the conclusion of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי holds the first קדושה was temporary (step 22).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא in his name, which is finished in step 26, says the opposite.

steps.title: Why would they need to make them holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the word 'made them holy,' since later in this same ברייתא it says no new holiness is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They made them holy, now?! But we say later on that there is no need to make them holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on one word in the second ברייתא, because it does not fit the end of that same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of this ברייתא (step 26) says the old holiness still works. If so, the returning exiles had no reason to make the cities holy again. So the word 'קידשום' cannot be right as written.

phrases.english: They made them holy, now?!
But we say later on
phrases.notes: Later in this same ברייתא, in the part quoted in step 26.

phrases.english: that there is no need to make them holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one word inside the ברייתא from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word וְקִידְּשׁוּם in the second ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא later says the first holiness lasts forever, so making the cities holy again would be pointless.

steps.title: They only listed them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the exiles found these cities and listed them. They did not make them holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they found these and listed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the wording of the ברייתא so it fits its own ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exiles did not create new holiness. They wrote down the cities they knew had walls from יהושע's time. That is why only these cities appear in the list.

phrases.english: Rather: they found these and listed them.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording: read 'listed them' in place of 'made them holy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exiles gave the cities new holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exiles only recorded the cities. Their holiness was already there.

steps.title: Any city known to be walled since יהושע counts
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא continues: any city with a family tradition of walls from יהושע's time has the walled-city laws, because the first קדושה lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only these. Any city about which you have a tradition from your fathers that it was walled since the days of יהושע בן נון follows all these laws, because the first קדושה made things holy for its time and also for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the second ברייתא. Here רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי clearly says the first holiness lasts forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the old holiness never ended, any city with a reliable tradition counts, even if it is not on the list. This is the direct opposite of what we learned from him in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition passed down from your fathers

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the source of the clash: the same תנא now says 'for the future,' while in step 22 he said 'not for the future.'

phrases.english: And not only these,
but any [city] about which you have in hand
a tradition from your fathers

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמּוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן –
phrases.english: that it was surrounded by a wall since the days of Yehoshua bin Nun –
all these מצוות apply in it,
phrases.notes: He means the special laws of a walled city.

phrases.english: because the first holiness made things holy for its time
and made them holy for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to quoting the second ברייתא from step 23, after the wording fix in steps 24 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any city with a tradition of walls from יהושע's time has walled-city status, because the first קדושה lasts forever.

steps.title: The two statements clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem: רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult: רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי contradicts רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now openly says the problem it has been building toward: the same תנא holds two opposite views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא he says the first holiness ended with the exile. In the second he says it lasts forever. Both cannot be his real opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי has two opposite statements. In one, the first walled cities lost their holiness. In the other, the first קדושה lasts forever. The גמרא now has to resolve this.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: [the statement] of Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosei
against [the statement] of Rabbi Yishmael bar Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר יוֹסֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the contradiction between steps 22 and 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two statements of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי can fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא says the first holiness was only for its time, and the other says it lasts forever.

steps.title: Two students reported his view differently
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: the two ברייתות are two different תנאים' reports of what רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי held.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: two תנאים disagree about what רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the contradiction. רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי did not contradict himself. Two later תנאים passed down his view in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that one person seemed to hold two opposite views. This answer keeps both ברייתות under his name. It says the disagreement is between the people who reported his view, not inside his own mind.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one possible answer, often one of several
Two תנאים (teachers from the time of the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here is saying רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי changed his mind. The point is that two people who reported his view disagree about what he actually said.

phrases.english: If you want, say: there are two תנאים
who disagree about the view of רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of the same teacher (תרי תנאי אליבא דפלוני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One person, רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי, held two opposite views.
steps.terutzMaskana: The contradiction comes from two different reports of his view, not from him.

steps.title: One of the teachings really belongs to his brother
steps.stepSummary: The second answer: one of the ברייתות was actually said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי, not by רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: one of the two ברייתות was said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: one of the ברייתות has the wrong name on it. The view that the first holiness lasts forever really comes from רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer removes the contradiction completely, because each view now belongs to a different person. רבי ישמעאל and רבי אלעזר are brothers, both sons of רבי יוסי, so mixing up their names is easy to understand. The גמרא now needs to show that רבי אלעזר really holds this view, and it does that in the next step.

phrases.english: If you want, say: one of them
phrases.notes: "One of them" means one of the two ברייתות we have been comparing.

phrases.english: was said by רבי אלעזר בר יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: חֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר יוֹסֵי אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות come from רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ברייתא comes from his brother רבי אלעזר בר יוסי, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Proof that רבי אלעזר בר יוסי holds the wall status stays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר בר יוסי reads the פסוק to mean that a city which once had a wall keeps its walled-city status.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בר יוסי says: "which has a wall" means even if it has no wall now, as long as it had one before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its second answer. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר בר יוסי clearly holds that walled-city status stays even after the wall is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לוא in the פסוק is written with an א, which could mean "no," but it is read as "has." רבי אלעזר learns from this that the city counts as walled even if it has no wall now. That fits the view that the first holiness lasts forever, so he is the right person to have said that ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction in רבי ישמעאל בר יוסי's words has two answers: either two תנאים reported him differently, or one ברייתא belongs to his brother רבי אלעזר בר יוסי. רבי אלעזר holds that a city that once had a wall keeps that status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the walled-city laws to the bigger question in the סוגיא: does the first holiness last forever?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר בר יוסי says:
"Which has a wall" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30. לוא is spelled with an א, like the word for "no," but it's read as "has."

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו
phrases.english: even though it does not have one now
but it had one before.
